newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche MG sees fall in Telekom borrowing.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche MG sees fall in Telekom borrowing.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said on Friday it expected a marked fall in the net indebtedness of telephone monopoly Deutsche Telekom AG by the year 2000.
In a report, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said it expected Telekom's net indebtedness to fall to 62.93 billion marks by the year 2000 from an estimated 92.17 billion marks this year.

"The management has made a clear commitment to ensuring that debt reduction takes precedence over further investments in other markets," Deutsche MG, the investment banking arm of Deutsche Bank AG, said in a study.
Deutsche is the main coordinator for Telekom's share flotation in November.
Deutsche MG predicted Telekom's indebtedness would fall to 86.05 billion marks in 1997, to 79.80 billion in 1998, and to 71.92 billion in 1999.
Deutsche MG also said it regarded an issue price of between 20 and 30 marks as appropriate, based on its valuation of the company.
